title: Mobile PageSpeed/Core Web Vitals overhaul (images, caching, render-blocking, robots/sitemap, contrast)

requirements.text: Replace above-the-fold critical image assets with modern compressed formats and update the app to prefer those formats to improve LCP/FCP without changing layout.

quotes: implement these changes directly in the project.

acceptanceCriteria: New optimized hero and logo assets exist in the repo as static files and are referenced by the UI.
Hero image still renders immediately on first load (no blank/flash), and its layout dimensions remain stable (no CLS regression).
All non-critical images remain lazy-loaded below the fold.

requirements.text: Update `frontend/src/components/OptimizedImage.tsx` to deliver responsive, non-blocking images: ensure priority images use `fetchpriority="high"` and eager loading; non-priority images use lazy loading; decoding is async; and WebP/AVIF are preferred with safe PNG fallback.

quotes: Improve image delivery — estimated savings 342 KiB

acceptanceCriteria: Priority images render with eager loading and high fetch priority, and non-priority images load lazily when near viewport.
When a browser supports WebP/AVIF it receives those; otherwise it receives the PNG fallback.
All images rendered through `OptimizedImage` include explicit width/height (or equivalent aspect-ratio stability) to avoid layout shifts.

requirements.text: Eliminate render-blocking and unnecessary work in `frontend/index.html`: update preloads to target the optimized hero asset, keep only truly critical preloads, and ensure analytics remains deferred and does not block first paint.

quotes: Eliminate render‑blocking requests — estimated savings 150 ms

acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/index.html` preloads the optimized hero asset used by the Hero component (and does not preload unused formats).
No additional synchronous scripts/styles are introduced that would block initial render.

requirements.text: Fix SEO robots.txt validity by serving a static `robots.txt` from `frontend/public/robots.txt` and ensure it includes a correct sitemap URL for `https://recomnowindia-2gi.caffeine.xyz/sitemap.xml`. Remove or bypass any React-route-based robots response that could cause crawlers to receive HTML/JS instead of plain text.

quotes: SEO: “robots.txt is not valid — 65 errors found.”

acceptanceCriteria: Requesting `/robots.txt` returns a plain-text robots file (not an HTML shell) when deployed.
The robots file contains `User-agent: *`, an allow rule, and a `Sitemap: https://recomnowindia-2gi.caffeine.xyz/sitemap.xml` line.
The SPA no longer relies on a React route that rewrites the document to produce robots.txt.

requirements.text: Fix sitemap delivery by serving a static `sitemap.xml` from `frontend/public/sitemap.xml` so crawlers can fetch XML directly without executing React. Ensure it uses `https://recomnowindia-2gi.caffeine.xyz/` as the base for URLs.

quotes: SEO: “robots.txt is not valid — 65 errors found.”

acceptanceCriteria: Requesting `/sitemap.xml` returns valid XML (not HTML/JS) when deployed.
The sitemap includes at minimum the homepage and key sections/anchors that are meaningful as standalone URLs (only include valid URL entries).
The SPA no longer depends on a React route that rewrites the document to produce the sitemap.

requirements.text: Improve cache efficiency for static assets using the existing service worker in `frontend/public/sw.js`: ensure generated image assets and build assets are cached with an appropriate cache-first or stale-while-revalidate strategy and that old caches are cleaned up reliably to reduce repeat-load transfer size.

quotes: Use efficient cache lifetimes — estimated savings 697 KiB

acceptanceCriteria: On repeat visits, core static assets (JS/CSS/logo/hero) are served from the service worker cache when available.
Cache versioning and cleanup prevents unbounded cache growth and removes outdated cached entries after deploys.
Robots.txt and sitemap.xml are not incorrectly cached in a way that would cause stale/invalid content to persist after updates.

requirements.text: Reduce main-thread work and TBT by ensuring heavy UI chunks remain code-split and only load on demand (admin panel, login, blog, toaster), and by removing any remaining production console logging via build configuration.

quotes: Avoid long main‑thread tasks — 13 long tasks

acceptanceCriteria: Non-critical UI modules remain lazy-loaded and do not increase the initial JS payload for the homepage route.
Production builds do not emit `console.log/info/debug` statements (confirmed by terser configuration behavior).

requirements.text: Resolve accessibility contrast warnings by adjusting the foreground/background color pairings (including muted text and gradient/button states) so text meets WCAG AA contrast on both light and dark themes without changing the overall brand feel.

quotes: Accessibility: “Background and foreground colors do not have a sufficient contrast ratio.”

acceptanceCriteria: Common text styles (body, muted text, button text, links) meet WCAG AA contrast on the default background in light mode.
Dark mode text contrast remains acceptable and no key UI text becomes harder to read.
Visual styling remains consistent with current brand gradients and theme variables (no layout changes required).

constraints: Do not edit files under `frontend/src/components/ui` (compose them instead).

Do not edit immutable paths: `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`, and `frontend/src/components/ui/*`.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in `backend/main.mo`; only add `backend/migration.mo` if state schema changes are required (not expected for these performance/SEO fixes).
nonGoals: Adding new product features or redesigning the site structure beyond what is required for performance/SEO/accessibility fixes.
Introducing third-party CDNs or external build pipelines beyond what the project already supports.
Implementing real-time features or adding new authentication providers.
